1 Angelo Mai edited these three fragments on war (Script. vet. nova collectio,
t. II, 1827, p. 675-7), using the Vatican codex 1056, of the 14th century (cf. Catal., IV, p. 102, no 2).
Which it seemed good to repeat here together with other excerpts of Julian, especially since
the text of the Angelicus codex is often more correct than Mai's edition, which sometimes can scarcely and
not even scarcely be understood.

summary.headline: Julian on War
summary.text: Astrological correspondences of the Sun, including colors, qualities, metals, plants, animals, humans, and products. Julian of Laodicea’s discussion of war explains how Ares, benefics and malefics, sect, sign condition, stations, and house positions determine whether war is just, lasting, glorious, and concerned with rule, life, harm, land, laws, race, or mutilation.
